explanation: Repair the checkpoint overflow, not the contact policy. Replace every persisted raw review response with a bounded point-only record retaining measurement frames, camera/pixel provenance, identities, errors and unresolved parameters; omit unused dense regions. Avoid duplicate baseline labels and final review parameters in alt.effect. The failed alt.model write is not assumed to exist. At the unchanged acknowledged frame 216, recover the supplied semantic review and reacquire its named depths without another identical GPT review or replaying any motion. If the frame differs, use the existing fresh-review path. Preserve the alternative-orientation screen, clearance and overlap margins, action-specific reviews, bounded controls and independent retention test.
interface: Patch the existing main(api); its return remains a JSON-compatible object with stage_status, reason, evidence, handoff and completion_proposed=false. Only alternate_pickup is implemented. Existing secure.* checkpoints remain untouched. alt.model stores compact local measurements and orientation screens; alt.progress stores acknowledged whole-lease/closing progress and compact revalidation; alt.effect stores the postclosure baseline, optional tracker provenance and differential lift evidence; alt.failure stores failed-action diagnostics. No additional checkpoint keys are introduced. Point records preserve world meters, depth, observation frame, camera, pixel and source. Dense regions are not persisted because this method does not consume them. Final observation parameters are stored once at alt.effect.effect_test.final_parameters; baseline landmark IDs remain at alt.effect.landmark_ids. The frame-216 recovered review is explicitly labelled and uses fresh point calls; it grants no action permission. Handoff retains actual state, checkpoint keys, provenance and limitations, with no subsequent-stage code.
jev_protocol:
The existing seven real-Jev questions are unchanged. Each x/y/z/rx/ry/rz instruction explicitly reads its state.processed_features.axes.<axis>.goal_relation: decrease means negative, within_tolerance means hold, and increase means positive. Translation choices refer to world coordinates; rotation choices refer to world rotation-vector components. The gripper question reads state.processed_features.objective.gripper and delivers open/close/keep unchanged. This method never requests reopening. Jev receives processed numerical gates, uncertainty and observation frames; it neither observes images nor calculates geometry.

All motion remains through api.drive or api.control. Drive uses at most 16 calls per lease, at most three leases per alignment/descent, phase-specific budget reserves, three steps per update, 0.008 m translation and 0.08 rad rotation bounds. Continuation after lease_exhausted requires measured whole-lease position gain above 0.0003 m or rotation gain above 0.003 rad. Stalls and ineffective corrections stop. High alignment and lift use 0.002 m position tolerance; contact descent uses 0.0005 m and 0.01 rad, included in the preserved geometric allowances. Independent action gates authorize alignment, descent, closure and lift separately. Closing remains one fixed-pose episode of at most four three-step controls, with actual counter-clearance checks. The lift can stop after a progressing first lease for effect assessment without claiming pose attainment.

Stage completion still requires fresh same-package identity, visible counter separation, retained opposed contact, hand rise at least max(0.020 m,6u), observed object rise at least max(0.015 m,4u), rotation at most 0.04 rad and geo.attachment_error at most 2u+0.002 m against actual hand motion. Optional tracking is replaceable by independently identified landmarks and requires fresh identity, at least 12 inliers, fraction at least 0.65, RMS at most 0.0015 m and spread exceeding three times its residual/noise allowance. Unknown tracking supplies no pose. Closure or tracking alone never proves retention. This repair adds no physical action and does not change any numerical acceptance margin.
